faqs.q: Does the brain surgeon salary include casual loading?

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Brain Surgeon Salary

When Australians search for a **brain surgeon salary**, they are typically looking at the earnings of neurosurgeons—medical specialists who perform surgery on the brain, spine, and nervous system. These professionals are among the highest-paid in the country, but their pay is governed by the Medical Practitioners Award 2020 (MA000031) from the Fair Work Commission. This article explains how to convert an hourly rate to an annual salary, what the award minimums are, and how tax and super affect take-home pay.

### How to Calculate Annual Salary from an Hourly Rate

The standard formula for converting an hourly rate to annual gross pay is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks = annual salary**

For full-time employees under the award, ordinary hours are 38 per week. So if you know the hourly rate, multiply by 38 and then by 52. For example, a Senior Specialist at Pay point 1 earns a minimum annual salary of $129,953, which works out to $66.64 per hour ($129,953 ÷ 38 ÷ 52). You can also calculate the fortnightly pay: weekly rate × 2. The weekly rate for that classification is $2,499.10 ($129,953 ÷ 52), so fortnightly pay is $4,998.20 before tax.

### Award Rates vs Market Rates for Brain Surgeons

The Medical Practitioners Award sets minimum salaries for each classification. For neurosurgeons, the relevant classifications are Specialist, Senior Specialist, Principal Specialist, and Senior Principal Specialist. The award minimums as of July 2026 are:

- Specialist Pay point 1: $129,953 per year ($66.64/hour)
- Senior Specialist Pay point 1: $129,953 (same as Specialist Pay point 1)
- Senior Specialist Pay point 2: $145,000 (approx.)
- Principal Specialist: $175,000 (approx.)
- Senior Principal Specialist: $200,000 (approx.)

However, many brain surgeons earn significantly more than the award minimum due to experience, private practice, or enterprise agreements. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) data from Jobs and Skills Australia, the median weekly earnings for full-time non-managerial neurosurgeons are well above the all-occupations average. The ABS also reports that 86% of neurosurgeons work full-time, averaging 57 hours per week. But for salary calculation purposes, we assume 38 ordinary hours unless overtime or additional agreements apply.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If a brain surgeon works as a casual employee, they receive a 25% loading on top of the ordinary hourly rate. For a Senior Specialist, that means $83.30 per hour ($66.64 × 1.25). The casual loading compensates for the lack of paid leave and other entitlements.

Superannuation is paid on top of ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a Senior Specialist on the minimum award rate, the employer would contribute an additional $15,594 per year into the super fund. For those earning above the base, super is capped at $32,499.60 (12% of $270,830).

### Tax on a Brain Surgeon Salary

Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds). A brain surgeon earning $200,000 per year would pay approximately $54,667 in tax plus $4,000 Medicare levy, leaving about $141,333 after tax. This is a rough estimate; actual tax depends on deductions, HELP repayments, and other factors.

### Using the Hourly to Annual Calculator

Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and see the annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures. You can also check the [pay guides](/blog) for the latest award rates. Remember that the calculator assumes a 38-hour week with no overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For casual employees, tick the casual loading checkbox to add 25% on top of the base rate.

### Key Takeaways

- The **brain surgeon salary** under the award starts at $129,953 per year for a Senior Specialist.
- To convert hourly to annual: multiply by 38 hours × 52 weeks.
- Super is 12% on top, capped at $270,830.
- Casual loading adds 25% to the hourly rate.
- Tax rates are progressive, and Medicare levy applies.

For a personalised estimate, use our calculator and refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman’s Medical Practitioners Award for exact classification rates.
